rules.title: Zero gradients in product UI
rules.fix: Flat token: the accent, or a Surface/* tint. For text, text-primary plus a weight step, or one word in text-accent.
rules.why: The competitor set ships zero gradients — flat is the expensive look, and a gradient is emphasis faked where hierarchy was the need.

rules.title: Indigo, violet and purple exist only as chart-4

detect.falsePositives: Still matches the Tailwind utility when it appears inside a comment or string that is quoting/discussing the banned class rather than applying it (e.g. an example in a code review comment). Every hit still needs a look, hence warning rather than blocker.

rules.fix: Remove it. Indigo/violet/purple are the model's default hue leaking through; if the need is a second categorical color, it is chart-4.
rules.why: Nothing in this system is purple. Its presence is machine provenance rather than a decision.

rules.title: Zero emoji in chrome
rules.fix: Use lucide-react at the size the component already imports (16/20/24), or drop the glyph — emoji live only inside user-generated content, never in chrome.
rules.why: Zero emoji in chrome — nav, buttons, headings, labels, bullets, table cells; the model's default is to reach for one, and it never belongs in generated UI.

rules.title: Motion only on state change — zero infinite loops outside genuine progress indicators
rules.fix: Delete it — bounce/elastic easing has no sanctioned use in this system; if the intent was a loading indicator, bind animate-spin to a real loading/uploading state instead.
rules.why: Zero infinite loops outside genuine progress indicators (Skeleton's pulse is the sanctioned exception); bounce easing specifically has no legitimate use anywhere in the system (MOT-3), so any occurrence is an automatic fail.

rules.title: Named transition properties, never transition-all
rules.fix: Name the properties that change — transition-colors, transition-transform, transition-opacity — at 120–150ms feedback or 200–250ms overlays, ease-out.
rules.why: transition-all animates layout properties by accident, which is both a jank source and an unstated decision.

rules.title: Say the thing — no generic CTAs
rules.fix: Name the object and outcome the control leads to — "Create submission request", "Import COI" — never a generic wayfinding label.
rules.why: Labels and CTAs name the object and outcome; the label predicts the next screen, and "Get Started"/"Learn More" predict nothing.

rules.title: Banned marketing register
rules.fix: Delete the adjective/claim, or replace it with the concrete mechanism it's standing in for — say what the feature does, not how impressive it is.
rules.why: elevate/unlock/empower/supercharge/seamless/effortless/game-changing and friends are marketing filler that fakes confidence a real description would earn. Downgraded to warning 2026-08-22: this repo's paywall/member-gate family (paywall-message.tsx, member-gate-row.tsx, hero-omnibox.tsx, media-prompt-bar.tsx, run-button.tsx, result-card.tsx, plus their tests) uses "unlock" as the literal, concrete gating mechanism — "Upgrade to unlock 4K export" names exactly what upgrading does — not marketing filler, and the pattern's existing \b(elevate|unlock)\b word-boundary cannot tell the two senses apart. Every current hit is this vocabulary (zero hits on the other terms); a genuine seamless/effortless/supercharge still surfaces, just as a warning rather than a blocker.

rules.title: Chart colors are chart-1…5, never library defaults
rules.fix: Assign chart-1…5 in order; the series answering the card's question gets emphasis, context series go gray.
rules.why: #8884d8 is recharts' default and an automatic fail — it is the clearest single tell of an unguided chart.

rules.title: Flat marks, hairline gridlines — never the recharts dash default
rules.fix: Delete the dash prop (or set an explicit hairline solid gridline) — this system's gridlines are hairline and horizontal-only, never dashed.
rules.why: Marks are flat: no glow, 3D, or gradient fills; the dashed "3 3" pattern is recharts' unstyled default leaking through, the same tell as the default palette.

rules.title: outline-none never ships without a focus-visible replacement

detect.falsePositives: Fires on outline-none whose focus-visible pairing lives on a different line or in a sibling class list, and on outline-none set on non-interactive containers (dialog/popover/collapsible content regions) that were never focusable. Both need a look before treating a hit as a real STA-3 violation.

rules.fix: Pair outline-none with the shared Focus Ring recipe (focus-visible:ring plus border-ring) on the same rule, or drop outline-none if the element was never interactive.
rules.why: Focus Ring token on every interactive element; outline-none without a :focus-visible replacement is the single most common way a control goes keyboard-invisible.
